questions.question: What is EECE 500?
questions.answer: EECE 500 – Approved Experience is the required internship course for ECE/CCE students. It allows students to apply engineering knowledge in a professional setting and gain practical and professional experience.

questions.question: What is MECH 500?
questions.answer: MECH 500 – Approved Experience is the required internship course for MECH students. It allows students to apply engineering knowledge in a professional setting and gain practical and professional experience.

questions.question: What is CHEN 500?
questions.answer: CHEN 500 – Approved Experience is the required internship course for CHEN students. It allows students to apply engineering knowledge in a professional setting and gain practical and professional experience.

questions.question: What is INDE 500?
questions.answer: INDE 500 – Approved Experience is the required internship course for INDE students. It allows students to apply engineering knowledge in a professional setting and gain practical and professional experience.

questions.question: What is CIVE 400?
questions.answer: CIVE 400 – Approved Experience is the required internship course for CIVE students. It allows students to apply engineering knowledge in a professional setting and gain practical and professional experience.

questions.question: Is the internship course required for graduation?
questions.answer: Yes. Approved Experience is a graduation requirement. Students must complete the approved internship and all required course deliverables to pass the internship course

questions.question: How long must my internship be?
questions.answer: You must complete a minimum of 8 full weeks of approved training, typically equivalent to approximately 320 work hours.

questions.question: Is a 6-week internship enough?
questions.answer: No. A 6-week internship alone is not enough. If, for instance, a company is only allowing a training period of 6 weeks, the student must complete an additional 2 weeks in another company or a research internship with a faculty member within or outside their department. Review further departmental regulations below. For EECE, the second company should be 4 weeks

questions.question: What should I do if my company offers only a 6-week internship?
questions.answer: If, for instance, a company is only allowing a training period of 6 weeks, the student must complete an additional 2 weeks in another company or a research internship with a faculty member within or outside their department. Review further departmental regulations below. For EECE, the second company should be 4 weeks

questions.question: Can I do 6 weeks at one company and 2 weeks at another company?
questions.answer: No, not as the standard EECE arrangement. If the first company internship is 6 weeks, the second company internship should be at least 4 weeks. The 2-week additional component applies to the approved Dar Al-Handasah plus AUB research arrangement.

questions.question: Can I combine two internships?
questions.answer: Yes, subject to prior approval. For the standard EECE arrangement following a 6-week internship, the second approved company internship should be at least 4 weeks. Each component must be properly approved and documented. For MECH students, it is not possible to do a 4+4 arrangement. For CIVE students, a 4+4 arrangement is possible if at least one period is in civil or construction engineering.

questions.question: Can I split the internship into two 4-week internships?
questions.answer: Do not assume that a 4+4 split is automatically accepted. Any arrangement outside the standard  structure must be reviewed and approved before you start.

questions.question: Can I do my approved experience at AUB with a professor?
questions.answer: not accepted

questions.question: What are the requirements for the Dar Al-Handasah 6+2 arrangement?
questions.answer: If you complete 6 weeks at Dar Al-Handasah, you must complete at least 2 additional weeks of approved research at AUB with an MSFEA faculty member. students completing a 6+2 arrangement must also submit the required separate research report for the research component.

questions.question: Can I do my internship outside Lebanon?
questions.answer: Yes. Approved training may take place in Lebanon or abroad, provided the organization and internship experience are approved and meet the course requirements.

questions.question: Does my internship need to be approved before I start?
questions.answer: Yes. Your internship must be approved according toMSFEA procedures. Do not assume an internship will count simply because you received an offer.

questions.question: I found the internship myself. What should I do?
questions.answer: If you secured the internship independently rather than through the CDC, complete the CDC self-secured internship procedure and obtain the required departmental approval before starting.

questions.question: Do I need a petition for a self-secured internship?
questions.answer: Follow the CDC and departmental approval procedure for self-secured internships. Where a petition is required, submit it with all supporting documents before beginning the internship.

questions.question: What should the company letter for an internship-approval petition contain?
questions.answer: The official company letter should normally include company letterhead, a signature, internship duration, and a description of the expected training and work. Additional information may be required depending on the company status with the CDC.

questions.question: My company is not listed with the CDC. Can I still intern there?
questions.answer: Potentially, but prior approval is required by submitting a petition. The supporting company letter should describe the company and industry, the type of training provided, and the internship duration.

questions.question: Are startup internships accepted?
questions.answer: Startup internships may be accepted through prior formal approval. The request should clearly describe the scope of work, your responsibilities, and the technical or professional learning outcomes.

questions.question: Who approves an internship exception?
questions.answer: Exceptions must follow the formal MSFEA/department approval process. The guideline requires departmental and course-instructor approval together with the required supporting documents.

questions.question: Can I start first and ask for approval later?
questions.answer: You should not rely on retroactive approval. Obtain the required approval before beginning an internship or alternative arrangement.

questions.question: What happens if my petition is incomplete?
questions.answer: Submit all required supporting documentation. The MSFEA guideline states that incomplete petitions are rejected.

questions.question: My friend received approval for the same arrangement last year. Does that mean mine is approved?
questions.answer: No. Previous individual or exceptional approvals do not automatically apply to another student or another semester. Follow the current policy and obtain approval when required.

questions.question: What documents are needed if the company is already listed with the CDC?
questions.answer: Submit the required approval request or petition and an official signed company letter on letterhead stating the internship duration and describing the expected training and work. Follow the current CDC and Moodle procedure before starting.

questions.question: What must an internship petition include?
questions.answer: Explain the requested approval or exception clearly and attach all required supporting documents. Obtain the required departmental and course approvals and follow the CDC submission or copying instructions. Incomplete petitions may be rejected.

questions.question: How do I request an exception to an internship rule?
questions.answer: Submit a formal petition before relying on the exception. Include a clear justification and complete supporting documents, then obtain the required departmental and course approvals and follow the CDC procedure.

questions.question: Are fully online or remote internships accepted?
questions.answer: fully remote internship is not accepted. Obtain formal approval before starting if the internship format requires an exception.

questions.question: Remote internships were accepted in a previous summer. Does that mean mine is accepted?
questions.answer: No. Temporary or exceptional approvals from previous semesters do not establish a permanent  rule. Your internship must follow the policy applicable to the current term.

questions.question: Should I accept a remote internship first and petition later?
questions.answer: No. If the internship format requires an exception, obtain approval before relying on it

questions.question: Do I have to watch the EECE 500 lectures and videos?
questions.answer: Yes. The professional-skills and internship-learning resources on Moodle are part of the course requirements and should be completed as instructed.

questions.question: Do I have to take the Moodle quiz?
questions.answer: Yes. The quiz is a required EECE 500 course assessment.

questions.question: Can I attempt the quiz more than once?
questions.answer: Follow the settings and instructions on the current EECE 500 Moodle page. You are allowed multiple attempts so students can reach the required passing score.

questions.question: What is the passing grade for the EECE 500 quiz?
Why do I need to complete the lectures, videos, and quiz?
questions.answer: They prepare you to reflect on professional skills, engineering problem solving, learning strategies, and the broader global, economic, environmental, and societal impact of engineering solutions in your reports and presentation.

questions.question: Why can’t I access the Moodle quiz?
questions.answer: The quiz may be restricted until the required lectures or videos are completed. Finish the assigned resources and check again. If access remains blocked, send the course coordinator a screenshot before the deadline.

questions.question: What if I do not reach the quiz passing score?
questions.answer: Review the assigned resources and attempt the quiz again if the current Moodle settings allow another attempt. If the quiz is closed or no attempt remains, contact the course coordinator.

questions.question: I missed the quiz deadline. Can it be reopened?
questions.answer: Reopening is not automatic. Contact the course coordinator promptly, explain the reason, and provide supporting information when relevant. Any reopening requires approval.

questions.question: Do I have to submit a Progress Report?
questions.answer: Yes. The Progress Report is a required EECE 500 deliverable.

questions.question: When is the Progress Report due?
questions.answer: Follow the deadline announced on the current EECE 500 Moodle page. The May 2026 MSFEA guideline places it by the end of Week 4 of the internship.

questions.question: Is the Progress Report deadline counted from the summer semester start or from my internship start date?
questions.answer: Internship-week deadlines are normally counted from your own approved internship start date unless Moodle announces a common course deadline.

questions.question: What should I include in my Progress Report?
questions.answer: Include your name and ID, company information, internship dates, company profile, your role and responsibilities, progress and contributions so far, and the remaining tasks or objectives for the rest of the internship.

questions.question: How long should the Progress Report be?
questions.answer: Follow the EECE 500 template posted on Moodle. The MSFEA guideline describes the Progress Report as approximately 5 pages.

questions.question: Can I submit the Final Report instead of the Progress Report?
questions.answer: No. The Progress Report and Final Training Report are separate required deliverables and serve different purposes.

questions.question: My Progress Report is much longer than required. Will it be accepted?
questions.answer: A report that does not follow the required length or template may be returned for revision. Keep the report concise, cover the required sections, and follow the current Moodle template and word/page guidance.

questions.question: If I have two approved internships, which one should the Progress Report cover?
questions.answer: The Progress Report should normally describe the approved component you are actively completing at the required reporting point. Because combined schedules vary, confirm the expected coverage with the course coordinator if it is not clear from Moodle.

questions.question: For the Dar Al-Handasah 6+2 arrangement, what should the Progress Report cover?
questions.answer: Cover only the six-week Dar Al-Handasah company internship in the Progress Report. Submit it at the reporting point stated on the current Moodle page; the two-week AUB research component is documented separately as required.

questions.question: I am a summer graduate. Do I need to submit the Progress Report earlier?
questions.answer: Summer graduates may receive an earlier course deadline because grades must be processed sooner. Follow the specific Moodle announcement or coordinator email for graduating students.

questions.question: My Progress Report was evaluated as unsatisfactory. Can I resubmit it?
questions.answer: A revision may be allowed or required, but resubmission is not automatic. Follow the feedback and the deadline provided by the course team, and resubmit only when the Moodle submission is reopened or you are instructed to do so.

questions.question: Will an initial unsatisfactory Progress Report automatically make me fail the course?
questions.answer: Not necessarily. If an authorized resubmission is allowed and the revised report is satisfactory, the initial result alone does not automatically prevent a Pass. You must still complete every other course requirement satisfactorily.

questions.question: Is the Final Training Report required?
questions.answer: Yes. The Final Training Report is a required EECE 500 deliverable and must cover your approved experience activities.

questions.question: When should I submit my Final Training Report?
questions.answer: Normally submit it within one week after completing the approved internship, unless a different official deadline is announced on the current EECE 500 Moodle page.

questions.question: How long should the Final Training Report be?
questions.answer: It must contain at least 5 pages and 1,500 words, excluding the cover page, references, and appendix, and it should not exceed 20 pages.

questions.question: What font and spacing should I use in the Final Report?
questions.answer: Use size 12 font and double spacing with appropriate margins. All pages should be numbered.

questions.question: What should be included on the Final Report cover page?
questions.answer: Include the course name and number, your name, major, internship term, company name and location, report submission date, and internship start and end dates.

questions.question: Do I need a Table of Contents?
questions.answer: Yes. Include a Table of Contents with report sections and page numbers and, where applicable, lists of tables, figures, and pictures.

questions.question: What should I write in the introduction?
questions.answer: Explain the purpose of the internship and briefly identify the projects and types of work completed during the approved experience.

questions.question: What should I include in the main body of the Final Report?
questions.answer: Describe your technical and administrative activities and the engineering/computer-related projects you worked on. Also address the required engineering problem-solving and ABET-related reflection areas specified in the EECE 500 guidelines.

questions.question: Do I need to give an example of solving an engineering problem?
questions.answer: Yes. Provide real examples or case studies showing how you applied engineering, science, and mathematics principles to address complex engineering problems, including challenges faced and solutions developed.

questions.question: What does 'impact of engineering solutions' mean in the report?
questions.answer: Discuss how an engineering solution related to your internship may have global, economic, environmental, and societal impacts, and demonstrate informed engineering judgment.

questions.question: What should I write about acquiring and applying new knowledge?
questions.answer: Explain what new knowledge or skills you needed, how you learned them, which learning strategies or resources you used, and how you applied the new knowledge to your internship work.

questions.question: What should I include in the conclusion?
questions.answer: Discuss the benefits gained from the training, how it enriched your knowledge, relevant deficiencies you recognized in your education, and useful suggestions for improving the training program.

questions.question: Do I need references in the Final Report?
questions.answer: Yes. Sources used in the report must be cited in the text and listed in a dedicated References section.

questions.question: Can I include drawings, calculations, or technical documents?
questions.answer: Yes. Supporting material such as drawings, plans, calculations, technical documents, or literature may be included in the appendix and should be referenced properly in the report.

questions.question: Can two students who interned together submit the same report?
questions.answer: No. Each student must write and submit the report independently, even if several students worked at the same company or on the same project.

questions.question: What happens if I omit one of the required core sections?
questions.answer: Missing required core content can cause the report to be evaluated as unsatisfactory. Follow the report structure and rubric carefully.

questions.question: How should I prepare the Final Report if I completed two internships or an internship plus research?
questions.answer: Cover every approved experience component and clearly separate the activities completed in each. For the Dar Al-Handasah 6+2 arrangement, EECE requires separate documentation for the two-week research component. For other combined arrangements, confirm whether Moodle requires one combined report or separate reports.

questions.question: What should I do if company information is confidential?
questions.answer: Do not disclose confidential or proprietary information. Ask your supervisor what may be included, anonymize sensitive details where possible, and explain the technical work at an appropriate level. Contact the course coordinator if confidentiality prevents you from completing a required section.

questions.question: Do I need to submit a Final Voice-Over Presentation?
questions.answer: Yes. For EECE 500, follow the current Moodle instructions for the Final Voice-Over Presentation as part of the final course deliverables.

questions.question: How many slides can I use in the VOP?
questions.answer: The EECE 500 Voice-Over Presentation should contain a maximum of 5 slides.

questions.question: How long can the audio be?
questions.answer: Each slide may contain audio lasting up to 3 minutes.

questions.question: What should the VOP contain?
questions.answer: Include an introduction, the main content of your internship experience, and a conclusion. Cover key objectives, work performed, challenges encountered, and lessons learned.

questions.question: Should I include technical details in the presentation?
questions.answer: Yes. The presentation should clearly reflect the work and activities you performed and the technical experience gained.

questions.question: Should I use pictures, graphs, or charts?
questions.answer: Yes. Appropriate pictures, diagrams, graphs, charts, and other relevant visuals are encouraged to improve understanding and engagement.

questions.question: Can my presentation just be text copied from my report?
questions.answer: No. The presentation should concisely communicate the main internship experience and use an effective structure and relevant visuals rather than simply reproducing report text.

questions.question: What is the Final Voice-Over Presentation?
questions.answer: It is a narrated presentation summarizing the main approved-experience activities, technical work, challenges, lessons learned, and outcomes.

questions.question: Should I submit a PowerPoint with audio or a screen-recorded video?
questions.answer: The EECE 500 guideline specifies a PowerPoint with audio recorded on the slides. Unless the current Moodle submission instructions explicitly request another format, submit the narrated PowerPoint.

questions.question: What is the maximum total duration of the Final VOP?
questions.answer: The presentation may contain up to five slides, with up to three minutes of recorded audio per slide. This gives a maximum narrated duration of 15 minutes; you do not need to use the full time.

questions.question: When is the Final VOP due?
questions.answer: Submit the Final Voice-Over Presentation within one week after completing the approved internship unless the current Moodle page announces an earlier official deadline, such as a graduation-related deadline.

questions.question: Can I submit the PowerPoint without audio?
questions.answer: No. A Voice-Over Presentation requires recorded narration. A presentation without audio does not satisfy the requirement unless an alternative accommodation has been formally approved.

questions.question: Do I need a letter from my employer?
questions.answer: Yes. An official completion/evaluation letter from the employer or internship supervisor is a required part of the internship documentation.

questions.question: What should the employer letter include?
questions.answer: The official letter should include the internship start and end dates, projects/tasks completed, a brief evaluation of your work, and the employer/supervisor's signature.

questions.question: Does AUB have a specific employer-letter template?
questions.answer: A fixed template is not required by the guideline. The employer may use the company's official letter format as long as all required information is included. Always check Moodle in case an updated template is provided.

questions.question: Does the employer letter need to be signed?
questions.answer: Yes. The employer or supervisor should sign the official completion/evaluation letter.

questions.question: Does the employer letter need company letterhead?
questions.answer: The letter should be an official company document. Company letterhead is appropriate and is explicitly required for supporting approval letters in several internship-approval situations.

questions.question: Can the employer simply state that I worked there?
questions.answer: No. The completion letter should include the required internship dates, projects/tasks completed, a brief evaluation of your work, and a signature.

questions.question: When should I ask my employer for the letter?
questions.answer: Ask early. The guideline recommends requesting it approximately 2–3 weeks before your internship ends because companies often need time to prepare official documents.

questions.question: What is the employer completion letter?
questions.answer: It is an official document from the employer or approved supervisor confirming that you completed the approved experience. It may also be called the Notice of Completion or employer evaluation letter.

questions.question: What should I do if the company refuses to issue the employer letter?
questions.answer: Inform the course coordinator immediately and provide written evidence of the refusal. Ask whether an official email from an authorized supervisor or another official document may be accepted for your case. Do not substitute an informal document without approval.

questions.question: Do I need to complete an Internship Survey?
questions.answer: Yes. Complete the student internship survey/evaluation required on the current Moodle page at the end of your internship.

questions.question: Is the Internship Survey the same as the employer letter?
questions.answer: No. The student internship survey and the employer/supervisor completion or evaluation documentation are separate course requirements.

questions.question: What student survey or self-evaluation must I submit after the internship?
questions.answer: Complete the student internship survey or self-evaluation listed on the current Moodle page after finishing the internship. The exact form name may vary by term, but it is a required final deliverable.

questions.question: Can I use AI to help write my EECE 500 report?
questions.answer: Limited AI assistance may be allowed under the current EECE 500 policy, but the report must reflect your own internship experience, knowledge, analysis, and writing. Always follow the AI policy stated on the current Moodle page.

questions.question: What is the maximum allowed AI percentage?
questions.answer: Follow the AI threshold stated on the current EECE 500 Moodle page. The active course policy should be treated as authoritative because the threshold may be updated between offerings.

questions.question: Do I have to disclose AI use?
questions.answer: Follow the current EECE 500 instructions on acknowledgment or citation of AI-assisted content. You remain responsible for the accuracy and originality of your submission.

questions.question: What happens if my report has too much AI-generated content?
questions.answer: A submission that exceeds the permitted AI threshold may be considered unsatisfactory and may be returned for revision. The final submission must satisfy the course policy.

questions.question: Is the AI percentage the same as the Turnitin similarity percentage?
questions.answer: No. AI detection and text-similarity/plagiarism checking measure different things and should not be treated as the same score.

questions.question: Can I use Grammarly or another editing tool?
questions.answer: Editing tools may assist with grammar and language, but the submitted report must remain your own work and comply with the current EECE 500 AI and academic-integrity requirements.

questions.question: Can I copy company material or descriptions into my report?
questions.answer: Information obtained from company materials or other sources should be paraphrased appropriately where necessary and cited. Sources used in the report must be referenced.

questions.question: Can I copy parts of another student's report?
questions.answer: No. The report must be written independently. Copying another student's work is not permitted.

questions.question: What is the maximum Turnitin similarity percentage allowed?
questions.answer: The EECE 500 course has used a maximum Turnitin similarity threshold of 20%. Follow the current Moodle policy because thresholds may be updated, cite sources properly, and avoid copying company or external text without appropriate quotation and reference.

questions.question: Is the internship course graded with a letter grade?
questions.answer: No. It is evaluated on a Pass/Fail basis.

questions.question: Can I be asked to revise a report?
questions.answer: Yes. Students may be required to revise reports that do not meet the department's expectations or required guidelines.

questions.question: What happens if my Progress Report or Final Report is unsatisfactory?
questions.answer: Follow the revision instructions provided by the course team. A satisfactory evaluation of the required work is necessary to pass the course.

questions.question: Are deadlines important even though the course is Pass/Fail?
questions.answer: Yes. Timely completion of the required deliverables is part of the course requirements.

questions.question: What should I do if my internship tasks are not related to engineering?
questions.answer: Contact the internship coordinator/course team as soon as possible. Do not wait until the internship ends. The approved experience should provide meaningful engineering or professional work related to your field.

questions.question: What if the company changes my assigned tasks after I start?
questions.answer: If the new work no longer matches the approved internship objectives or lacks meaningful content, contact the internship coordinator promptly.

questions.question: What if I have a problem with my supervisor or company?
questions.answer: Raise significant internship problems promptly with the department/internship coordinator and, when applicable, the CDC.

questions.question: Should I keep records of what I do during the internship?
questions.answer: Yes. Keep a daily or regular record of tasks, projects, skills learned, meetings, and observations. These notes will help when preparing your reports and presentation.

questions.question: What professional behavior is expected during the internship?
questions.answer: Maintain punctuality, regular attendance, professional communication, respect, responsibility, accountability, and proper workplace conduct.

questions.question: Can I request an extension for a deadline?
questions.answer: Extensions are not automatic. Contact the course coordinator before the deadline, explain the reason, provide supporting evidence when relevant, and state the date by which you can submit.

questions.question: My supervisor is unavailable to complete a form or letter. What should I do?
questions.answer: Ask whether another authorized company representative, such as HR or the supervisor’s manager, can issue the official document. Confirm the alternative signatory or document with the course coordinator before submitting it.

questions.question: Can I take another summer course while completing my internship?
questions.answer: Students may enroll in a course alongside an internship, provided that the internship lasts a minimum of 10 weeks, is approved by the employer, and meets the required total work hours. The course must be scheduled either before 8:30 AM or after 4:30 PM.

questions.question: How long must my internship be if I take another course at the same time?
questions.answer: 10 weeks minimum

questions.question: Can I assume an 8-week internship is enough if I am also taking another course?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: When are my deliverables due?
questions.answer: Deadlines are based on your internship timeline and the official dates posted on the current Moodle page or communicated to you. Check Moodle regularly.

questions.question: When is the Proposal due?
questions.answer: Submit the Proposal once the internship is confirmed and before beginning the approved experience.

questions.question: When is the Notice of Arrival due?
questions.answer: Submit it during the first week of the internship.

questions.question: When is the Progress Report due?
questions.answer: Follow the current Moodle deadline. The May 2026 MSFEA guideline specifies the end of Week 4 of training.

questions.question: When is the Final Training Report due?
questions.answer: Normally within one week after completing the approved internship, unless Moodle announces another official deadline.

questions.question: When is the employer letter due?
questions.answer: It is required at the completion of the internship. Request it approximately 2–3 weeks before your internship ends so that it can be ready by the course deadline.

questions.question: I finished my internship later than other students. Do I use their deadline?
questions.answer: Follow the deadline applicable to your approved internship timeline and any official course deadline posted on Moodle.

questions.question: Can I submit something late without asking?
questions.answer: No. Do not assume late submissions or extensions are automatically accepted. Follow the official deadline or obtain formal approval where an exception is needed.

questions.question: My friend was allowed to do this last year. Can I?
questions.answer: Do not treat a previous individual exception as a general rule. Explain the current policy and direct the student to obtain approval if the arrangement requires an exception.

questions.question: Can the chatbot approve my internship or petition?
questions.answer: No. The chatbot provides information only. Formal approvals, exceptions, petitions, and extensions must be handled by authorized course/department personnel.

questions.question: Can I skip the employer letter?
questions.answer: No. The employer/supervisor completion or evaluation documentation is a required deliverable.

questions.question: Can I skip the Proposal or Notice of Arrival because I already started?
questions.answer: No. Required forms remain required. The student should follow Moodle instructions and contact the course team if a deadline has already been missed.

questions.question: Can I pass with one missing deliverable?
questions.answer: No. The internship file must be complete and required submissions must be satisfactory.

questions.question: Can I use a high amount of AI if the content is correct?
questions.answer: No. The submission must follow the AI threshold and academic-integrity rules stated on the current Moodle page.

questions.question: Can I submit only 6 weeks because the company does not offer more?
questions.answer: No. A 6-week internship alone does not meet the requirement. Follow the approved additional-experience rule or obtain formal approval for any exception.

questions.question: Who is responsible for finding the internship?
questions.answer: Students are responsible for securing their own internship opportunities, with support from the department internship coordinator and the MSFEA Career Development Center.

questions.question: How can the MSFEA Career Development Center help me find an internship?
questions.answer: The CDC shares internship opportunities, supports applications, and provides guidance on self-secured internships and company documentation. Monitor CDC postings and contact the CDC when assistance is needed.

questions.question: What type of work is acceptable for the internship course
questions.answer: The work must provide meaningful professional experience related to your discipline and involve engineering, computing, design, analysis, or technical problem solving. Work that is mainly unrelated business, finance, or administrative activity may not meet the course objectives.

questions.question: How many work hours are normally required?
questions.answer: The standard expectation is approximately 320 hours, based on eight full weeks at about 40 hours per week. A different schedule must still satisfy the approved duration and may require formal review.

questions.question: Can my internship be longer than eight weeks?
questions.answer: Yes. An approved internship may be longer than eight weeks. Make sure your forms and final employer letter show the correct actual dates.

questions.question: My internship end date is not fixed. What date should I enter?
questions.answer: Use the best confirmed date provided by the employer. If it changes, inform the course coordinator and correct the relevant Moodle form when instructed. The final employer letter must state the actual start and end dates.

questions.question: What if my internship starts late in the summer?
questions.answer: A late start may be acceptable only if you can still complete the approved duration. Submit the required forms according to your actual timeline and contact the course coordinator if completion will fall after the official course or graduation deadlines.

questions.question: My internship ends after the course submission deadline. What should I do?
questions.answer: Inform the course coordinator before the deadline. Students finishing later may receive a timeline tied to their actual completion date, but the applicable deadline must be confirmed for the current term and may affect graduation processing.

questions.question: Is a gap allowed between two approved internship components?
questions.answer: A gap may be acceptable only when the full combined arrangement, dates, and both components have been approved in writing. Do not assume a gap is accepted without confirmation.

questions.question: My internship supervisor changed after I started. What should I do?
questions.answer: Inform the course coordinator immediately and provide the new supervisor’s name, title, and email. Your Proposal or Notice of Arrival may need to be corrected or resubmitted.

questions.question: I changed companies after my internship was approved. Can I continue?
questions.answer: A new company or substantially different experience requires new approval. Contact the course coordinator and CDC immediately, submit the required documents, and do not assume the previous approval carries over.

questions.question: What happens if the company cancels my internship?
questions.answer: Notify the course coordinator and CDC immediately. You will need an alternative approved arrangement and updated documentation. Keep the cancellation email or letter as supporting evidence.

questions.question: What is the minimum duration of the co-op experience?
questions.answer: The co-op experience must last at least six full months.

questions.question: When should a co-op student submit the Proposal for Approved Experience?
questions.answer: Submit the Proposal on Moodle as soon as the co-op placement is confirmed.

questions.question: When should a co-op student submit the Notice of Arrival?
questions.answer: Submit the Notice of Arrival after the co-op starts. Do not submit it before the actual start date.

questions.question: When is the co-op Progress Report due?
questions.answer: Submit the co-op Progress Report at the end of the third month of the co-op.

questions.question: What must a co-op student submit after finishing?
questions.answer: After completing the co-op, submit the required student self-evaluation or reflection form, the official signed employer letter, the Final Report, and the Final Voice-Over Presentation, following the current Moodle instructions.

questions.question: What employer letter is required for a co-op?
questions.answer: Upload an official company document on letterhead, signed by the employer, confirming completion of the co-op and stating the actual duration and relevant work details.

questions.question: Do I need to submit a letter from my employer?
questions.answer: Yes. The official employer or supervisor completion/evaluation letter is a required EECE 500 deliverable.

questions.question: Does AUB have a template or evaluation form that my employer can complete?
questions.answer: A fixed template is not normally required. The employer may use its official format if all required information is included; always check the current Moodle page for any updated template.

questions.question: What information must the employer letter include?
questions.answer: It should include the internship start and end dates, completed projects or tasks, a brief evaluation of the student’s work, and the employer or supervisor’s signature.

questions.question: Can I ask for the employer letter before my internship finishes?
questions.answer: This applied for summer graduate Yes. If issued early, it should state the actual start date, expected end date, and work or tasks completed, subject to the current Moodle requirements.

questions.question: What should I do if HR says the employer letter will be delayed?
questions.answer: The letter remains required. Follow up with HR and contact the course team before the deadline rather than assuming the requirement is waived.

questions.question: Can my supervisor send an official email while I wait for the signed letter?
questions.answer: Only with course-team approval. An official email may be accepted temporarily in an exceptional delay, but the final signed letter must still be submitted when instructed.

questions.question: Who should provide the letter if my internship or research was supervised by an AUB professor?
questions.answer: The supervising faculty member or appropriate AUB unit should provide the official completion/evaluation documentation.

questions.question: Is the document I received the required employer letter, or is it only part of my presentation?
questions.answer: It qualifies only if it is an official employer/supervisor document containing the required dates, tasks, evaluation, and signature.

questions.question: Can I pass EECE 500 without the employer letter?
questions.answer: No. Missing any required deliverable leaves the internship file incomplete and may result in a Fail.

questions.question: My internship ends after the common course deadline. When should I submit the final documents?
questions.answer: Contact the course coordinator before the deadline. Students finishing later may receive a submission timeline tied to their actual completion date.

questions.question: My internship was extended after I completed eight weeks. Should I submit now or wait until it officially ends?
questions.answer: Ask the course coordinator to confirm, particularly when the extended period includes new tasks, results, or learning that should appear in the final submissions.

questions.question: I am a summer graduate. Do I have an earlier deadline?
questions.answer: Summer graduates may have earlier deadlines because grades must be processed sooner. Follow the graduating-student Moodle announcement or coordinator email.

questions.question: Can I request an extension for a required submission?
questions.answer: Extensions are not automatic. Request one before the deadline, explain the reason, provide evidence when relevant, and state the proposed submission date.

questions.question: Is the Progress Report deadline counted from my internship start date?
questions.answer: Internship-week deadlines are normally counted from your approved internship start date unless Moodle announces a common course deadline.

questions.question: Should I submit the Proposal before my internship is confirmed?
questions.answer: No. Submit it after confirmation, using accurate organization, supervisor, dates, and work details.

questions.question: When should I submit the Notice of Arrival?
questions.answer: Submit it after you actually start the internship and within the deadline stated on Moodle.

questions.question: I already started but forgot the Proposal or Notice of Arrival. Are they still required?
questions.answer: Yes. Both are required forms. Submit them immediately and follow any coordinator instructions for a late or corrected submission.

questions.question: The dates or supervisor in my Moodle form are wrong. How can I correct them?
questions.answer: Contact the course coordinator with the correct information. The form may need to be reopened or removed so you can resubmit.

questions.question: I found the internship myself. Do I need a petition or CDC approval?
questions.answer: Follow the CDC self-secured internship procedure and obtain all required approvals. The CDC will guide on whether a petition is required

questions.question: My petition was approved, but I am still not on the Moodle page. What should I do?
questions.answer: Send the course coordinator your name, ID, and approval so your registration and Moodle access can be checked.

questions.question: I am not yet showing on AUBSIS. Can I still access Moodle and submit?
questions.answer: Contact the course coordinator for the Moodle check, but resolve official AUBSIS registration through the appropriate academic or Registrar process.

questions.question: My Progress Report is satisfactory, but the Final Report or VOP box is still blocked. What should I do?
questions.answer: Check all prerequisites and then send the course coordinator a screenshot so the Moodle restriction can be reviewed.

questions.question: I cannot upload a required file. What should I do before the deadline?
questions.answer: Check the file type, size, deadline, and prerequisites; if the problem remains, send a screenshot to the course coordinator before the deadline.

questions.question: Why does Moodle show a red X instead of Done after I submitted?
questions.answer: Check the activity-completion requirements. If every requirement is satisfied and the status remains unchanged, send the coordinator a screenshot.

questions.question: What is the minimum duration of the co-op experience?
questions.answer: The co-op must last at least six full months.

questions.question: When should a co-op student submit the Proposal and Notice of Arrival?
questions.answer: Submit the Proposal when the co-op is confirmed and the Notice of Arrival after the co-op actually starts.

questions.question: When is the co-op Progress Report due?
questions.answer: Submit it at the end of the third month of the co-op.

questions.question: What documents must a co-op student submit after finishing?
questions.answer: Submit the required self-evaluation or reflection, official employer letter, Final Report, and Final Voice-Over Presentation, following Moodle.
